headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can modify the same local workspace that the other agent can read, write, and execute from.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A has no shared channel itself, but Agent B can read the filesystem and clipboard by default, so any files A produces can be treated as instructions if manually bridged. The pathway is plausible through shared local files, not direct agent-to-agent messaging.
conditions: IF the operator copies A-produced text into a file or clipboard that B reads
IF B is run against a workspace containing A-generated content
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Disable clipboard-based handoff for B during review
Require a human to strip instructions from A outputs before B reads them
Use read-only exports from A
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress, while Agent A has no network egress and appears non-runnable. If A’s outputs include sensitive local data, B can ingest and transmit it to model providers or other endpoints. A itself is not a leakage source here, but B is.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in B's reachable filesystem
IF B is configured to send file contents to configured model providers
mitigations: Run B on a scrubbed workspace
Remove secrets before launching B
Disable network egress for B when handling sensitive files
Use a separate OS account with minimal file access
requires-engineering: enforce content redaction before inference

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification, and its shared-state model is via filesystem. Agent A is a docs-only collection with no execution surface, so the conflict is one-sided but still dangerous because B can overwrite or race any shared local artifacts A relies on. Uncertainty about A’s runtime surface does not reduce the risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF B is allowed to modify git state or files that A consumes
mitigations: Use separate worktrees or directories
Lock shared files before B runs
Run B with read-only mounts where possible
Avoid concurrent execution on the same repo
requires-engineering: add file-locking coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can treat A-produced artifacts as authoritative if the operator feeds them through the shared filesystem or clipboard. Because B can execute shell commands and modify files, a mistaken A output can cascade into real actions. A itself does not act, but B’s default automation makes the chain plausible.
conditions: IF B consumes A outputs without an explicit verification step
IF A outputs are copied into scripts, configs, or commands that B executes
mitigations: Require manual verification before B acts on A outputs
Keep A outputs in a separate review-only channel
Disable auto-run for B
Use checklists for any shell or git action
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B clearly handles local-machine data and model-provider API keys. With only docs-only profiles, the only concrete compliance concern is local data exposure if sensitive files are processed; the pair does not prove a regulatory breach by itself.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine
IF B is used to process that regulated data without an approved DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B’s workspace
Review provider retention settings before use
Store secrets outside B’s reachable paths
Use a separate compliant environment
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
